question: Liberalisation reduced government control over economic activities. What did liberalisation in 1991 primarily aim to eliminate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial licensing and quota system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Liberalisation in 1991** aimed to eliminate the **industrial licensing and quota system**, which had restricted the growth and development of industries in India.
 
• The **licensing system** required businesses to obtain prior approval from the government to set up, expand, or diversify industries, creating bureaucratic hurdles.
 
• The **quota system** limited the production capacity of industries by prescribing fixed production levels, thus hindering economic growth.
 
• The 1991 reforms led to the removal of most of these restrictions, enabling industries to operate freely and efficiently, fostering competition and innovation.
 
• By reducing **government control**, liberalisation paved the way for private sector participation and foreign investment, accelerating India's economic growth trajectory.
